title: OpenAI Proves Seymour’s 1990 Second-Neighborhood Conjecture, Corroborated by Specialist Reproof
whyItMatters: Resolves Paul Seymour’s 36-year-old Second-Neighborhood Conjecture for all finite oriented graphs—one of the flagship OpenAI math proofs to earn an independent specialist human reproof (Nov 24, 2026).
summary: Released as entry #173 of OpenAI’s openai/math collection (dated September 23, 2026), an internal OpenAI reasoning model produced a complete proof of Paul Seymour’s 1990 Second-Neighborhood Conjecture: every finite oriented graph contains a vertex whose second out-neighborhood is at least as large as its first. Assuming a hypothetical counterexample exists, the AI proof amplifies the violation into strict subset inequalities that force a counting objective past its maximum. On November 24, 2026, independent graph-theory specialists posted a short alternative reproof combining OpenAI’s reduction with a streamlined out-neighborhood growth argument—elevating the result from the bulk catalog into independently corroborated territory.
technicalHighlights: Resolves Paul Seymour’s 1990 conjecture (|N^{++}(v)| ≥ |N^+(v)| for some vertex v) across all finite oriented graphs without degree or tournament restrictions.
Avoids prior minimum-degree and median-order bottlenecks by amplifying a putative counterexample into a contradiction on a global subset counting objective.
Supported on November 24, 2026 by an independent short specialist reproof validating and streamlining OpenAI’s core reduction.
caveats: Both OpenAI’s September 23 manuscript and the November 24 specialist reproof are unrefereed preprints awaiting formal journal peer review and full Lean certification.

scoreRationale.foundational: Settles one of the best-known open conjectures in directed graph theory since Paul Seymour posed it in 1990.
scoreRationale.ripple: Proves that genuine, human-verifiable breakthroughs emerged from OpenAI’s autonomous mathematics pipeline and could be rapidly digested and shortened by specialists.
scoreRationale.verification: Substantially stronger than an unreviewed bulk dump thanks to the independent November 24 specialist reproof, though journal refereeing is still pending.
scoreRationale.velocity: Solved a stubborn 36-year-old extremal graph theory conjecture autonomously.
